messages:
maya: quick proposal — we should move from a single global trace TTL to a retention_by_env model. idea: short warm window for fast queries + a cheaper cold archive for long tails. outline below, want takes before i make a PR.

alex: +1 to per-env. we need clear guardrails so someone doesn't accidentally set prod to 90d and kill query perf / cost. can we tie it to per-route SLA?

maya: yeah exactly. proposal sketch: dev=7d, staging=30d, prod: warm=14d (hot index), cold=365d (object archive). routing: traces older than warm -> move to cold blob storage, keep minimal index for id lookup.

sanjay: big question: what do we mean by "minimal index"? full span index is huge — suggest we only keep trace_id + service list + root_ts in index for cold traces. no full span text. reduces ES cost by ~8x in our estimates.

zoe: only concern is debugging long-tail errors where we need span context. if we remove spans from index, we'll have to fetch and hydrate from cold blob which adds minutes. for oncall use we should provide a one-click "rehydrate" flow. ux: button on console triggers fast restore of that trace to warm storage for X hours.

harper: putting config idea here to discuss (very rough):
```yaml
telemetry:
  traces:
    retention_by_env:
      dev: 7d
      staging: 30d
      prod:
        warm_window: 14d
        cold_window: 365d
    cold_index_fields: [trace_id, service_names, root_timestamp]
exporters:
  archive_s3:
    bucket: "rwd-trace-archive-prod"
    region: us-west-2
  realtime_es:
    host: "es-realtime.internal"
```

maya: + note: exporter fanout — otel collector should write in parallel to realtime ES (for warm) and to archive_s3 with lifecycle rules. we need idempotent movers so we don't double-charge.

alex: also add a per-tenant quota on cold storage growth rate. otherwise a noisy customer could fill the archive and spike costs. quota could be enforced via a daily allowance and alerts.

sanjay: agree on quotas. also propose adaptive sampling for prod: keep 100% of error traces, 10-20% of successful traces for after-warm window. that reduces cold write volume a lot.

zoe: how about query UX? console search should default to warm window and show a banner "Search older traces" that will run a cold lookup (slower). we should show expected time-to-restore when user asks to rehydrate.

maya: ops question: what happens during incident when we need bulk access to old traces? we could temporarily promote a time range to warm, but need fast copy path. is there infra to do mass rehydrate?

harper: infra-team note: we have a job that can bulk copy S3 objects back into the warm bucket, but it wasn't built for on-call scale. we can extend it to accept time ranges and tenant filters, but it needs RBAC + rate limit to protect ES.

infra-bot: scheduled: retention-policy-smoke-test job queued (job id: rwd-ret-smoke-2026-03-24). will run nightly against dev/staging.

alex: next steps i think: 1) costs model for indexing options (full vs minimal), 2) estimator for cold write volume with adaptive sampling, 3) UX spec for rehydrate + RBAC flows. maya can you spin up a PR with the yaml sketch and perf numbers?

maya: on it — i'll draft the RFC and link cost spreadsheet. will ping when PR is ready. :thumbsup:

zoe: thanks — small ask: include a couple example oncall playbooks for "rehydrate trace during incident" so SREs can practice.

sanjay: also add metric: cold-read latency SLO (e.g., 60s median for initial fetch) so we can track improvements.

maya: noted. thanks all.
__note: This document is a single Slack thread. Messages are chronological and prefixed by sender name.
